Lessons.Title: Beyond 100,000
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will read, write, and represent numbers within 1,000,000 using base-ten blocks, diagrams, and expanded form.
In previous grades, you used base-ten blocks, diagrams, and expanded form, a specific way of writing a number as a sum of hundreds, tens, and ones, to represent numbers within 1,000. In this lesson, you extend your understanding of place value to write and represent numbers within 1,000,000. The reasoning you use helps to develop conceptual understanding of expanded form, allows them to practice reading and writing large numbers, and prompts them to think about the relative value of each place.
Core relationship: Regrouping base-ten blocks to represent up to 1,000,000. If the small cube stands for 10 instead of 1, every block's value becomes ten times as large.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  How Many Do You See?	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Lin’s Representation (15 minutes); Activity 2:  What Number is Represented?	 (10 minutes); Activity 3:  Build Hundred-thousands	 (10 minutes); Cool-down: Represent 234,000 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: A diagram originally models 15,710. What value would all blocks represent if every unit is now worth ten times as much?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): A block was 100 when the unit cube meant 1; what is its value when the unit cube means 10?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.
